questions.q: Distinguish between tertiary, quaternary and quinary activities.
answer: As economies develop, activities beyond farming and manufacturing become more important, and these are grouped into tertiary, quaternary and quinary activities.

answer.text: Tertiary activities make up the service sector. Instead of producing goods, they provide services such as trade and commerce, transport, communication, banking, insurance, tourism, health and education. They rely on skills and labour rather than raw materials.

Quaternary activities form the knowledge sector, concerned with the collection, production and spread of information. They include research and development, information technology, consultancy and finance, and require highly trained people.

Quinary activities are the highest level, involving the making of important decisions and the use of specialised, high-level knowledge. They are carried out by top executives, policymakers and leading scientists, and are sometimes called gold-collar professions.

answer: Thus these activities move from providing everyday services to handling knowledge and taking key decisions.
